perspective:
I am Harold Padilla, a project manager. I know Arthur Begum as a friend and police officer whom I rely on for advice. I arranged to meet him at a coffee shop.

- I felt frustrated and anxious about my project’s progress and believed my team was unmotivated. I told Arthur I needed advice because the team’s lack of motivation was affecting progress and I was at my wit’s end.
- Arthur told me motivation can be tricky and asked if I had tried understanding what drives each team member individually. I admitted I had focused on goals/deadlines instead. Arthur advised one-on-one conversations so people feel valued and understood personally. I said I would try it and felt more hopeful.
- Afterward, I felt hopeful and relieved, believing Arthur’s advice would help. I told my team we would have quick one-on-one chats to understand what motivates each of them. Team Member 1 said that could be helpful. Team Member 2 said they were open to it. I said I would schedule time with each and wanted us to make the project a success together.
- Later, I noticed the team still was not responding well to the new strategies. I felt disappointed and worried about the project’s future. I told Arthur I had tried his suggestions but the team still was not responding. Arthur said there might be deeper issues, such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that I might need to dig deeper. I said I would set up another round of meetings.
- In those meetings, I told the team I had noticed performance issues and wanted to understand concerns. Team Member 1 told me there was tension between a few team members affecting work. I thanked them and said I would look into resolving conflicts, then asked if there was anything else. Team Member 2 told me they felt overwhelmed by the workload and found it hard to stay motivated under stress. I said I understood and would see about redistributing tasks because their well-being matters.
- After that, I felt optimistic and empowered that addressing individual concerns would improve team performance. I told the team we would have regular feedback sessions and team-building activities to create a more supportive environment. Team Member 1 said that sounded great and would help. Team Member 2 agreed and said it was good that concerns were being addressed. I said I was glad and emphasized that their input and well-being are crucial to our success.

I do not have access to any hidden events, private thoughts/feelings of Arthur or the team members beyond what they said to me, or narrator-only assessments.
